title: EKS control-plane Terraform connector + upgrade-watchdog (declarative provisioning + self-heal)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current priv-EKS Terraform modules focus on initial provisioning but lack a concise declarative connector pattern and an automated watchdog that supervises upgrades and rolls back unsafe changes. This ticket implements a new 'connector' module that acts as a single source of truth for control-plane lifecycle operations and an upgrade-watchdog subsystem that validates post-upgrade invariants and triggers automated safe rollbacks when health gates fail.

Scope:
- Deliver a new terraform module (redwood_priv_eks_connector) that exposes a slim, opinionated interface for: VPC attachments, control-plane kms encryption config, control-plane tags & metadata, kube-admin bootstrap token secrets rotation, and upgrade policies.
- Implement an upgrade-watchdog component (Terraform-managed Lambda + CloudWatch Events) that runs post-apply health checks and reports pass/fail with automatic rollback anchors (Terraform state snapshot + S3).
- Add idempotency tests, preflight validations, and deterministic drift assertions to the module's test harness.
- Provide outputs and a concise consumption example for Private control plane provisioning (module versioning: semver >= v0.3.0).

Acceptance criteria:
- Module API surface documented in README with example usage and minimal variables.
- All idempotency tests pass in CI (apply -> plan -> apply no-op).
- Upgrade-watchdog triggers on control-plane version changes, runs 3 health probes (API responsiveness, node readiness, certificate validity), and performs a safe rollback when any probe fails for >2 consecutive runs.
- Terraform state snapshotting implemented and replayable for rollbacks.
- KMS cross-account key usage validated in a privileged test account.
- PR reviewed by infra and security, merged, and published to the registry with changelog entries.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Connector vs operator: We intentionally avoid running a controller inside customer clusters for the control-plane lifecycle; instead the module wires a lightweight, infra-side watchdog (Lambda) that can be centrally monitored and is easier to reason about in air-gapped setups.
- Rollback approach: Using S3-stored tfstate snapshots + automation reduces blast radius. We considered snapshotless rollbacks (terraform rollback) but it's not atomic across multiple accounts. Snapshot approach gives reproducible recovery.
- Health probes: Keep probes simple (kube-apiserver liveness, etcd member count, certificate expiry threshold) to minimize false positives. More complex app-level checks belong in Console-level monitors.

Outputs (examples):
- control_plane_endpoint
- control_plane_certificate_thumbprint
- state_snapshot_s3_key
- upgrade_watchdog_lambda_arn

Security considerations:
- Lambda role limited to s3:GetObject/PutObject on a restricted bucket and eks:Describe* on specific cluster ARNs.
- Use envelope encryption with customer KMS key (optional) for state snapshots.
- Security review flagged for cross-account KMS usage (ticket referenced below).

Testing and rollout plan:
1) Merge module behind feature flag and publish as prerelease v0.3.0-rc.1 in registry.
2) Run controlled canary: apply to 3 nonprod clusters across regions, trigger simulated upgrades, assert watchdog behavior.
3) Iterate on probe thresholds, then promote to v0.3.0.

Migration notes for existing consumers:
- Provide shim example showing how to switch from legacy redwood_priv_eks_bootstrap to redwood_priv_eks_connector. Minimal variable mapping required (vpc_id, cluster_name, kms_key_arn).

Related docs and artifacts:

- RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1PrivEksConnectorRFC
- Prototype repo (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-eks-connector
